chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad Abu Yusuf al-Khazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: When there is an heir from among those who have a legislated share, then he has greater right to the wealth.

key_terms.أَحَقّ: More deserving/has greater right — denotes legal precedence in inheritance
key_terms.فَرِيضَة: Legislated share — the fixed portion assigned by Quranic text to certain heirs (e.g., spouse, children, parents)
key_terms.وَارِث: Heir/inheritor — one who inherits from a deceased person

ai.seo_question: Who has greater right to inheritance when there is an heir with a legislated share in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Ali (AS) establishing a foundational rule of Islamic inheritance law: an heir with a legislated (Quranic) share (farida) takes precedence over residual heirs. This ruling reflects the Quranic system of inheritance (mirath) where certain family members are assigned fixed portions. The original audience — jurists and students of fiqh in early Islamic Kufa — would have understood 'farida' as referring specifically to the shares fixed in Quran 4:11-12 and 4:176.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad Abu Yusuf Al Khaaz, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘When there was an inheritor from the one for him is an Obligation (legislated share), so he is more deserving of the wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub from Hammad abu Yusuf al-Khazzaz from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’
Amir al-Mu’minin would say, ‘An heir who has an ordained share is more deserving of the legacy.’”
